scope: Actual production immediate-PPU decoder, source-bound literal/fill/alias semantics, pinned native output and independent bundled CPU-produced PPU comparisons, relocation and format variants, unsupported/false-positive refusal, bounded work and noninterference. Derivatives are structural tests, not independent engines. No browser or hardware evidence.

results.name: Native literal/fill construction yields independently pinned background and palette data
Decoded bytes equal actual CPU-created PPU nametable and palette at the initialization return
Meaningful literal, palette and CHR edits remain recognized without the original source hash
Palette aliases keep hardware last-write semantics and physical source provenance
Final PPUCTRL selects either physical background CHR bank, without guessing tile usage
A relocated constructor is followed through its actual reset JSR, despite an old matching copy
The same construction decodes from NROM-256 upper PRG with shifted physical provenance
Zero-count X loops mean 256 writes and the parser accounts for every destination
Each final nametable value cites its last writer, including the title overlay
Unreachable matching construction and an unknown initializer remain unknown
Near-matching branch, addressing, return and coverage failures cannot produce an importable background
Unknown poll results cannot supply control literals and NMI cannot precede final display setup
Unsupported PPUDATA increment, NMI, final nametable and display masks are refused
Constructor work and output are bounded even for a small source with repeated full-page rewrites
Malformed containers, trainers, CHR RAM and unsupported mappers stay outside this decoder
All pure decode outcomes preserve original bytes, authored project, history and emulator
